title: Type predicates
description: Learn how user-defined type guards let you narrow types safely and make React components more robust.

data.text: TypeScript can narrow many types with built-in checks like `typeof` and `in`, but those only go so far. When you work with custom classes, union types, or objects from an API, you need your own narrowing logic. Type predicates, also called user-defined type guards, let you write a function that tells the compiler exactly which type a value is.

A type predicate is a special return type in the form `value is Type`. When the function returns `true`, TypeScript treats the input as that type inside the calling code. It is one of the cleanest ways to move runtime checks into reusable helpers.

data.title: Simple Type Predicate
data.content: Checking if a value is a string

data.text: The real power of type predicates shows up with object shapes. You can check for a unique property and tell the compiler the full object type. This is especially useful for API responses that may return different shapes depending on status.

data.title: Checking API Response Shapes
data.content: Type predicate for API response discrimination

data.text: React components frequently receive mixed data from context, props, or external APIs. Type predicates let you validate that data once and then use it safely without repeated `as` assertions.

data.title: Guarding Event Payloads
data.content: Type predicate for a custom event payload

data.title: Keep Predicates Honest
data.text: A type predicate should always return true only when the value truly matches the claimed type. A bad predicate can create a false sense of safety and allow runtime errors to slip through.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Type predicates use the return type `value is Type`
They let you write reusable runtime checks
Use them for API responses, custom events, and complex unions
Keep predicate logic simple and accurate
data.takeaway: Type predicates let you move validation logic out of components and into small, testable helpers.
